theme-accent.note: Resolved by the user's Telegram client; the hex is only the outside-Telegram fallback.

theme-button.note: Fill of a selected chip. Selection is a fill, never a hue shift.

statement-ink.note: Body text and every figure not carrying status.

margin-grey.note: Where most of the interface lives: captions, meta lines, disabled arrows.

hairline.note: Every 1px rule in the system. Falls back through the hint color because section-separator-color is Bot API 7.6+.

paper.note: The page and the tab bar. Opaque: content scrolls beneath the bar.

card-paper.note: Cards rest on top of the page: Telegram's own page/section split.

positive-green.note: Derived, not fixed. Mixed toward the theme's text color: 4.82:1 light, 6.34:1 dark. Only ever the Neto.

negative-red.note: Prefers Telegram's destructive color, then mixes. 6.50:1 light, 4.83:1 dark. Only ever the Neto.

ledger-green.note: The income series. Fixed because Telegram exposes a destructive color and no positive one.

slot-1.note: Categorical identity: the card and the trend line must match.

kpi.purpose: Money inside a card. 1.75rem is a ceiling: $1.234.567,00 fits a 360px card at this size and not at 2rem.

table.purpose: The Evolucion grid only. At body size six months plus the category column measure 372px and overflow a 360px phone.

label.purpose: KPI captions, movement meta lines, chip text, chart legends. Always Margin Grey.

micro.purpose: The Variacion note and the Evolucion legend. The floor - nothing goes smaller.

cursor.purpose: The period header's chevrons only. Glyphs, not text: the size is what makes one character readable inside its own 44x44 tap target.

shadows.name: sticky-column-edge
shadows.purpose: Structural, not atmospheric: stands in for the border a collapsed table takes away from a sticky scrolling cell. The only shadow in the system.

motion.name: content-loading
motion.purpose: #content drops to 0.55 opacity while an htmx request is in flight. The entire loading vocabulary.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Chart animation is disabled outright rather than shortened.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The design target. Not a breakpoint the CSS branches on - the width every measurement was checked against.

breakpoints.name: pico-grid-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: Pico's .grid becomes one column below this. The app is never wider, so cards are always full-width.

components.name: KPI Card
components.description: A caption over a large tabular figure. The Neto variant is the only element in the app that carries a status color.
components.css: .ds-kpi { background: var(--pico-card-background-color, #fff); border-radius: 0.25rem; padding: 0.75rem; } .ds-kpi-label { font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--pico-muted-color, #646b79); margin: 0 0 0.15rem; } .ds-kpi-figure { font-size: 1.75rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; margin: 0; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--pico-color, #373c44); } .ds-neto-good { color: color-mix(in srgb, #0ca30c 70%, var(--pico-color, #373c44)); }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Period and currency selection. Selected is a fill, not a hue shift - Pico's one-step shift measures 1.32:1 in dark.

components.name: Tab Bar
components.description: Fixed bottom navigation. The active tab carries a 2px bar as well as color, because muted grey against the accent is only 1.47:1.
components.html: ResumenCuentasEvolucion

components.name: Variacion Callout

components.name: Evolucion Heat Cell
components.description: The one dense surface. Two shading steps of the theme accent against the row's own average; the mix caps at 45% so text on a cell stays legible.

components.name: Failure State
components.description: One of three wordings, each with its own way out. Silence is not an option: without a message the loading opacity reverts and the tap reads as ignored rather than failed.
components.html: Sin conexión. Probá de nuevo cuando vuelva.

components.name: Tappable Target
components.description: The single shared 44x44 tap-target rule. Applied in markup to the account card; the tab link, period cursor arrows and chip still carry their own hand-written copy of the same floor rather than the class, which is how the chip row -- the most-tapped control in the app -- was the one missed for as long as the rule lived only by hand.
components.css: .ds-tappable { min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }

components.name: Accounts Total
components.description: Cuentas' running total, above the account cards and outside the .grid. Takes the KPI figure treatment (1.75rem/600) directly, since the scoped .grid article .money rule cannot reach it and this is the number that governs the whole screen.
components.css: .ds-accounts-total { font-size: 1.75rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; margin: 0 0 var(--pico-spacing, 0.75rem); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

narrative.overview:
The Mini App is a statement that closes. Every screen exists so the number at the top can be explained by the rows underneath it, and the user can walk from a total down to the individual movement that produced it without ever losing the window they were reading. Trust is the deliverable: a figure that does not reconcile is worse than no figure at all.

The app does not own its palette. Telegram does. Every color token is a var(--tg-theme-*) reference with a fallback, so the surface is painted in whatever theme the user chose in their client - including a custom one this system has never seen. That inverts the usual relationship: brand does not live in hue here, because hue belongs to the user. It lives in density, in the tabular figure, and in the discipline that every number reconciles.

The material is deliberately thin. Pico CSS 2.1.1 provides the base, app.css adds roughly 430 lines of scoped corrections, and every one of them exists because something specific broke on a 360px Telegram webview. The system is a stack of small, argued repairs, not a theme.
keyCharacteristics: Telegram-themed: 19 Pico color tokens are remapped onto --tg-theme-*, each with a fallback, so the app follows the user's client and still works outside it.
Flat and tonal: depth is a 1px hairline border and a card background, never a decorative shadow.
Tabular numerals everywhere money appears, so columns of figures stay comparable.
44px minimum on everything tappable - tabs, period arrows, account cards.
No web fonts, no build step, no CDN: every dependency is vendored and pinned under static/.
Color is reinforcement, never the only channel: the active tab carries a 2px bar, the default account carries a star with an aria-label.

rules.name: The Theme-Follows-The-User Rule
rules.body: A color literal in app.css is a bug unless one of the three documented exceptions covers it (account slots, the income series, the tap-highlight). Every var(--tg-...) carries a fallback - a missing one does not fail loudly, it paints the element transparent or black, and only outside Telegram, where nobody is looking. TestAppCSS_EveryTelegramVarHasFallback enforces this.

rules.name: The Three Contexts Rule
rules.body: Pico defines its palette in three theme contexts. The remap must appear in all three, each with that theme's own fallbacks. One plain :root block loses on specificity; one high-specificity block wins everywhere and then its single-theme fallbacks override Pico's dark palette outside Telegram, silently turning dark mode light.

rules.name: The Mixed Status Rule
rules.body: The Neto pair is derived, never fixed: color-mix(in srgb, <hue> 70%, var(--pico-color)). Measured, the fixed values gave 3.35:1 and 3.75:1, passing AA only as large text; mixed at 70% the four cases measure 4.82, 6.34, 6.50 and 4.83. The pair is asymmetric on purpose: red prefers Telegram's destructive color, green has no counterpart to prefer.

rules.name: The One Status Rule
rules.body: Positive Green and Negative Red appear on exactly one element per screen: the Neto figure. Variacion de saldos is deliberately uncolored - a positive variation can be a CEDEAR that rose or a load that was missing, and tinting it green would assert something the system does not know.

rules.name: The Categorical Exception Rule
rules.body: Account slot colors stay fixed hexes while everything else follows the theme. There, color is identity - the card and the trend line must match - and deriving eight mutually distinguishable hues from an arbitrary user theme is not a solvable problem.

rules.name: The Reinforcement Rule
rules.body: No meaning is carried by color alone. The active tab gets a 2px geometric bar; the default account gets a star glyph with an aria-label; the Evolucion heat cells cap their mix at 45% so text on them stays legible.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything that is money wears .money. No exceptions, including inside table cells and inline balance lines.

rules.name: The Truncation Rule
rules.body: A movement's title and its meta line each truncate to one line with an ellipsis. A long merchant name may never push the amount off the right edge - the amount is the reason the row exists.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Anything tappable is at least 44x44: tab links, period arrows, account cards, chips. .tappable is the one shared rule for this, applied in markup to the account card; tab-link, the period arrows and .chip still carry their own hand-written copy of the same floor rather than the class. A card that opens a drill still declares its own floor even when its content would be shorter.

rules.name: The Rows-Not-Tables Rule
rules.body: A list of movements is a stack of section.mov-group day groups -- each headed by a GroupTitle and holding a ul.mov-list of that day's rows -- not a table. GroupRowsByDay splits the list into consecutive same-date runs; the date lives once on the group header and rows carry only what varies within a day. Evolucion is the one real table, and it pays for it with a horizontal scroller and a sticky first column.

rules.name: The Carried-State Rule
rules.body: Every view emits AppState - a hidden #app-state block of inputs the tab bar reads with hx-include. A view that renders without it silently resets the user's period on the way out, because periodFromQuery never 400s. A view may carry the state without showing the controls, but it may not skip it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest, and a shadow must earn its place by solving a real layering problem the way the sticky column's inset does. Whether a genuinely floating layer may use an ambient shadow is undecided - the app has no such layer yet.

dos: Do reach for a Pico custom property before writing a literal color. They are already mapped to the user's Telegram theme, so both themes and every custom one work for free.
Do give every var(--tg-...) a fallback, always. Outside Telegram there is no failure - just a transparent or black element nobody sees.
Do mirror any new theme mapping across all three of Pico's theme contexts.
Do put .money on every monetary figure, wherever it renders.
Do give anything tappable a 44x44 minimum and a deliberate pressed state.
Do carry every meaning in a second channel besides color - a glyph, a label, or geometry like the active tab's 2px bar.
Do emit @AppState(p) from every view, even one with no period controls.
Do write the reason in the CSS when you override Pico. Every existing override says what broke; a silent one gets cleaned up by the next person.
Do derive a footer total from an aggregate over all rows, never from the rows on screen - the list is capped at 50.
donts: Don't write a fixed color for anything but the three documented exceptions: account slots, the income series, and the tap-highlight rgba.
Don't send a color from Go to a chart. Send a role and resolve it in app.js; that is what keeps chart data following the theme.
Don't derive account slot colors from the theme. Color is identity there, and eight distinguishable hues cannot be pulled out of an arbitrary theme.
Don't add a web font. system-ui is the stack; a webview on a bad connection cannot wait for a download to render text that is mostly numbers.
Don't load anything from a CDN or add a build step. Vendor and pin it under static/, the way htmx 2.0.4, Pico 2.1.1 and Chart.js are.
Don't add a decorative box-shadow, gradient, or backdrop blur. Depth is a 1px border and a background.
Don't color the Variacion figure - or any figure other than Neto - with a status hue.
Don't turn a movement list into a <table>, or take the horizontal scroller off Evolucion.
Don't use the hidden attribute to hide a .mov-row; display: flex beats it.
Don't go below 0.75rem for text, or above 1.75rem for a figure inside a card.
